faqs.q: Sec. 14-5. - Interference with animal management officer unlawful.
faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be unlawful for any person intentionally to interfere with, hinder, harass,
               molest, injure, obstruct, or disobey a lawful order from any animal management officer
               in the discharge of his official duties under this chapter or other applicable law.
(b)
It shall be unlawful for any person to fail to allow or to refuse entry to an animal
               management officer demanding entry for purposes of inspection pursuant to
section 14-4
(e) and (f).
(c)
It shall be unlawful for an owner or custodian to fail to produce an animal that must
               be made available to an animal management officer within 24 hours of the issuance
               of a summons and complaint under
section 14-202
(c). Failure to produce the animal will be considered interference with an officer.
(Code 1981, § 6-5; Ord. No. 3496, § 2, 12-14-1998;
Ord. No. 4878
, § 3, 10-7-2024)
